title: Doherty Threshold — UI Visual Feedback Under 400ms
description: Productivity and user engagement soar when a computer and its users interact at a pace (< 400ms) that ensures neither has to wait on the other. Every button click, filter toggle, or form submission must deliver immediate visual feedback (< 100–400ms) via Optimistic UI, `:active` state transitions, or instant skeleton placeholders.
vision_prompt_heuristic: Verify that interactive buttons and controls have distinct immediate feedback states (active/pressed styling, optimistic state transitions, or progress indicators) so users never wonder if their click registered.
remediation_guide: Implement Optimistic UI for fast mutations (likes, add-to-cart, tab switches), transition button states to `loading` within `< 50ms` via `useOptimistic`, and offload heavy computations from the main thread.

title: Postel's Law — Liberal Input Acceptance & Programmatic Normalization
description: 'Be conservative in what you send, be liberal in what you accept from others.' Input fields for phone numbers, credit cards, tax IDs, postal codes, dates, and currency amounts must never fail validation due to user-entered spaces, dashes, parentheses, or country prefixes (`+1 (555) 123-4567` vs `15551234567`). Parsing and sanitization must happen in application code rather than forcing formatting effort onto the user.
playwright_check_snippet: const inputs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input[type="tel"], input[name*="phone" i], input[name*="card" i], input[name*="zip" i], input[name*="postal" i]')); if (!inputs.length) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; const overlyStrict = inputs.filter(i => { const pat = i.getAttribute('pattern'); return pat && pat === '^[0-9]+$' && (i.maxLength > 0 && i.maxLength <= 11); }); return overlyStrict.length === 0 ? 'APPLIED_PASS' : 'VIOLATED_FAIL';
vision_prompt_heuristic: Inspect any form fields on the page (phone, credit card, date, postal code). If no form fields exist, return DOES_NOT_APPLY. Check if error messages or helper text punish users for entering spaces, dashes, or parentheses.
remediation_guide: Remove restrictive HTML attributes such as `pattern="^[0-9]{10}$"` and tight `maxlength` caps that truncate pasted spaces. Normalize input values in code before validation (`const cleanValue = rawValue.replace(/[\s\-()]/g, '');`) and format display masks automatically.

title: Von Restorff Isolation Effect — Single Visually Dominant Primary CTA per Viewport/Card
description: When multiple similar objects are present, the one that differs from the rest is most likely to be remembered and acted upon. Within any single viewport or distinct card/dialog container, there must be strictly one visually dominant Primary CTA (high-contrast solid accent fill), while secondary actions use Outline/Secondary or Ghost/Tertiary styling.
playwright_check_snippet: const buttons = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('button, a[role="button"], input[type="submit"]')).filter(b => { const r = b.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.top >= 0 && r.bottom <= window.innerHeight && r.width > 60 && r.height >= 36; }); if (!buttons.length) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; return 'APPLIED_PASS';
vision_prompt_heuristic: Examine the primary viewport screenshot. Count how many competing high-saturation solid-filled Primary CTA buttons fight for attention in the hero section or active modal. Pass if there is a clear singular primary focal action and secondary actions are visually subordinate; fail if multiple loud primary buttons compete equally.
remediation_guide: Structure buttons across three explicit hierarchy tiers: `Primary` (solid accent fill `bg-primary text-on-primary` — max 1 per screen/dialog), `Secondary` (`border-outline bg-transparent`), and `Tertiary` (`bg-transparent text-muted`).

title: Gestalt Proximity & Common Region — Label-to-Input Distance < 50% of Inter-Field Gap
description: Under Gestalt psychology (Law of Proximity and Law of Common Region), objects placed close together are perceived as a single functional unit. The vertical distance from a `<label>` to its associated `<input>` must be less than 50% of the vertical gap between the previous input field and that label (e.g., 4–6px from label to input vs 16–24px between separate form groups).
playwright_check_snippet: const labels = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('label')); if (labels.length < 2) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; for (let i = 1; i < labels.length; i++) { const prevInput = labels[i-1].control || labels[i-1].nextElementSibling; const currInput = labels[i].control || labels[i].nextElementSibling; if (prevInput && currInput) { const lRect = labels[i].getBoundingClientRect(); const iRect = currInput.getBoundingClientRect(); const pRect = prevInput.getBoundingClientRect(); const labelToInput = Math.abs(iRect.top - lRect.bottom); const prevToLabel = Math.abs(lRect.top - pRect.bottom); if (prevToLabel > 0 && labelToInput >= prevToLabel * 0.65) return 'VIOLATED_FAIL'; } } return 'APPLIED_PASS';
vision_prompt_heuristic: Inspect any forms or card groups on the page. If no forms or grouped content exist, return DOES_NOT_APPLY. Verify that each label sits unmistakably closer to its own input field than to the field above it, and related sections are clearly bounded by whitespace or subtle borders (Common Region).
remediation_guide: Wrap each `label + input + helper-text` unit in a `.form-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; }` container, and space sibling field groups via `.form-stack { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 20px; }`.

title: Miller's Law (5–9 Top-Level Nav Items) & 4-Digit Alphanumeric Chunking
description: The average human working memory holds 7 ± 2 items (Miller's Law) and up to 4 active chunks (Chunking). Top-level ungrouped navigation menus must not exceed 5–9 items, and long numeric strings (credit cards, phone numbers, IBANs, order numbers) must be visually formatted into 3–4 character chunks.
playwright_check_snippet: const navItems = document.querySelectorAll('header nav > ul > li, header nav > a'); if (navItems.length === 0) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; return navItems.length <= 9 ? 'APPLIED_PASS' : 'VIOLATED_FAIL';
vision_prompt_heuristic: Examine the top-level navigation bar, category lists, and any displayed numeric strings (order IDs, phone numbers, prices). Verify that top-level navigation has <= 9 items and dense information is chunked into scannable groups of 3-5 items.
remediation_guide: If top-level navigation exceeds 7–9 links, consolidate secondary destinations into categorized mega-menus or drawers. Format long numeric strings using `Intl.NumberFormat` and 4-digit regex grouping.

title: Serial Position Effect & Zeigarnik / Goal-Gradient Progress Indicators
description: Users best recall and locate the first and last items in a sequence (Serial Position Effect: placing Brand/Catalog first and Profile/Cart/Primary CTA last in navigation bars). Under the Zeigarnik and Goal-Gradient Effects, incomplete multi-step flows (onboarding, checkout, wizards) must display an explicit step progress indicator (`Step 2 of 4` or a progress bar with endowed initial progress) to accelerate task completion.
playwright_check_snippet: const nav = document.querySelector('header, nav'); if (!nav) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; return 'APPLIED_PASS';
vision_prompt_heuristic: Check two ergonomics patterns: 1) In the primary navigation bar, verify that the most important brand/home link and primary conversion/account action occupy the first and last positions (Serial Position Effect). 2) If a multi-step flow, onboarding, or checkout is shown, verify that a clear step progress indicator is visible.
remediation_guide: Anchor primary entry points and conversion CTAs at the far-left and far-right edges of headers and bottom tab bars. In multi-step flows, render `<ol aria-label='Checkout steps'>` with `aria-current='step'` and a visual completion bar.

title: ISO 9241-110:2020 Dialogue Principles — Task Suitability, Controllability & Error Robustness
description: ISO 9241-110:2020 Ergonomics of Human-System Interaction mandates 7 dialogue principles: 1) Suitability for the user's tasks (zero unnecessary inputs or steps), 2) Self-descriptiveness (clear labels and statuses without external manuals), 3) Conformity with user expectations (consistent terminology and conventions), 4) Learnability, 5) Controllability (user-paced interaction, no auto-advancing carousels without pause, explicit Back/Cancel), 6) Use error robustness (error prevention and forgiving recovery), and 7) User engagement.
vision_prompt_heuristic: Evaluate the interface against ISO 9241-110:2020 Controllability and Self-Descriptiveness: confirm there are no forced auto-rotating carousels without pause controls, no dark-pattern confirmshaming modals, and all interactive controls clearly communicate their purpose.
remediation_guide: Remove non-essential fields from conversion forms (Suitability for the task), provide explicit 'Back / Cancel' actions at every dialog step (Controllability), and display inline format examples prior to validation errors (Use error robustness).
